newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Restructuring drives Electrolux to loss.
newsitem.headline: Restructuring drives Electrolux to loss.

text.p: Swedish appliance maker Electrolux Wednesday posted a loss of 264 million crowns ($32.6 million) for the first half of 1997, citing hefty restructuring costs of 2.5 billion crowns ($308 million).
The market had expected a loss of 305 million crowns ($37.6 million).

Electrolux said sales in the six months to June 30 were flat at 57.27 billion crowns ($7.07 billion) against 57.01 billion crowns ($7.03 billion) a year ago, when it posted a profit of 1.81 billion crowns ($223 million).

Chief Executive Michael Treschow, who initiated the tough restructuring drive in June, said the second quarter of the year had seen some improvements and better markets for white goods, especially in North America.
Even so, operating income from the group's major appliance division fell over the period.
Treschow said higher sales in several European countries contributed to a 5 percent increase in total group sales after adjustment for exchange rate effects in the second quarter.
